raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Thank you @cmlccie for the extraordinarily detailed report and root-cause analysis — the GPU-free grammar reproducer made this very actionable.

## Summary

Under `tool_choice="auto"`, a single tool with `"strict": true` put **every** tool under the model-native structural tag, including non-strict ones (`function_call_parser.py`: `any(tool.function.strict ...)`). For `qwen3_coder`, that tag cannot produce the chat template's own zero-argument form (`<function=NAME>\n</function>`), and a non-strict tool compiles to an open parameter zone — so the model invents arguments for non-strict zero-argument tools (4/4 runs in the report).

A structural tag is triggered per tool call and lists every allowed tool name, so it cannot enforce per-tool strictness. This PR constrains under `"auto"` only when **every** tool is strict (or `SGLANG_TOOL_STRICT_LEVEL >= FUNCTION`, which is documented as "constraints for all tools"). A mixed set now leaves generation unconstrained, exactly like the no-strict case — matching OpenAI's per-tool `"strict"` semantics. Trade-off, as noted in the issue: in a mixed set, the strict tool's schema is not enforced under `"auto"` (it still is under `"required"`/named `tool_choice`, which is unchanged).

## Change

- `python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py`: `should_constrain_auto` now requires `all(...)` instead of `any(...)` for the tool set (with an empty-tools guard preserving prior behavior); comment documents the rationale and trade-off.
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py`: 3 new tests covering the mixed-strict scenario from this issue (`qwen3_coder` and `kimi_k2` auto → no constraint; all-strict auto → structural tag).

## Before / after (copy-paste-runnable, xgrammar==0.2.7, no GPU)

This drives the **real** `FunctionCallParser.get_structure_constraint` from this repo against `xgrammar.get_model_structural_tag(model="qwen_3_coder", ...)` with the issue's exact tool set (`get_schema`: no args, `strict: false`; `query_database`: required `sql`, `strict: true`):

```
=== FunctionCallParser.get_structure_constraint('auto'), mixed strict set ===
BEFORE (any strict -> constrain):  ('structural_tag', <StructuralTag>)   # the buggy tag
AFTER  (all strict required):       None                                  # unconstrained, = no-strict control

=== Grammar acceptance of the tag SGLang requested BEFORE the fix ===
  template-native zero-arg  "<tool_call>\n<function=get_schema>\n</function>\n</tool_call>"  accepted=False
  invented <parameter=sql>  "<tool_call>\n<function=get_schema>\n<parameter=sql>\n\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>"  accepted=True
```

Unchanged behavior, verified against the real code:
- `all strict + auto` → `('structural_tag', <StructuralTag>)`
- `no strict + auto` → `None`
- `mixed + required` → `('structural_tag', <StructuralTag>)` (strict schemas still enforced for required/named calls)

## Tests

- New unit tests in `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py::TestGetStructureConstraint` (mixed → `None` for `qwen3_coder`/`kimi_k2` under `auto`; all-strict `qwen3_coder` under `auto` → `structural_tag`): 3 new + 4 neighboring existing assertions pass.
- The GPU-free grammar reproducer above reproduces the reported acceptance table for the pre-fix tag.

Fixes #45235.

files.patch:
@@ -293,8 +293,19 @@ def get_structure_constraint(
             or None if no constraint applies.
         """
         is_required = tool_choice == "required" or isinstance(tool_choice, ToolChoice)
+        # Under "auto", constrain with the structural tag only when every tool
+        # is strict. A model-native structural tag is triggered per tool call
+        # and lists every allowed tool name, so it cannot enforce per-tool
+        # strictness: putting a mixed set under one tag would also constrain
+        # the non-strict tools with their open (non-strict) schemas, which can
+        # corrupt their calls (e.g. qwen3_coder's tag masks the template's own
+        # zero-argument form and lets the model invent parameters for a
+        # non-strict tool, sgl-project/sglang#45235). A mixed set therefore
+        # leaves generation unconstrained, exactly like the no-strict case,
+        # matching OpenAI's per-tool "strict" semantics. The strict tools'
+        # schemas are still enforced under "required"/named tool_choice.
         should_constrain_auto = tool_choice == "auto" and (
-            any(tool.function.strict for tool in self.tools)
+            (bool(self.tools) and all(tool.function.strict for tool in self.tools))
             or self.tool_strict_level >= ToolStrictLevel.FUNCTION
         )

@@ -5285,6 +5285,100 @@ def test_kimi_auto_no_strict_returns_none(self):
         result = parser.get_structure_constraint("auto")
         self.assertIsNone(result)
 
+    def _make_mixed_strict_parser(self, parser_name):
+        """Two tools mirroring sgl-project/sglang#45235: a non-strict
+        zero-argument tool alongside a strict tool."""
+        tools = [
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="get_schema",
+                    description="Return the database schema.",
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {},
+                        "additionalProperties": False,
+                    },
+                    strict=False,
+                ),
+            ),
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="query_database",
+                    description="Run a read-only SQL query.",
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {"sql": {"type": "string"}},
+                        "required": ["sql"],
+                        "additionalProperties": False,
+                    },
+                    strict=True,
+                ),
+            ),
+        ]
+        from sglang.srt.function_call.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser
+
+        return FunctionCallParser(tools, parser_name)
+
+    def test_qwen3_coder_auto_mixed_strict_returns_none(self):
+        """auto with a mixed strict/non-strict tool set must not constrain.
+
+        Forcing non-strict tools under the qwen_3_coder structural tag makes
+        zero-argument tools receive invented arguments
+        (sgl-project/sglang#45235). "strict" is per-tool per OpenAI semantics.
+        """
+        parser = self._make_mixed_strict_parser("qwen3_coder")
+        result = parser.get_structure_constraint("auto")
+        self.assertIsNone(result)
+
+    def test_kimi_auto_mixed_strict_returns_none(self):
+        """auto with mixed strictness behaves like the no-strict case."""
+        parser = self._make_mixed_strict_parser("kimi_k2")
+        result = parser.get_structure_constraint("auto")
+        self.assertIsNone(result)
+
+    def test_qwen3_coder_auto_all_strict_returns_structural_tag(self):
+        """auto with every tool strict keeps the structural_tag constraint."""
+        import xgrammar as xgr
+
+        tools = [
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="get_schema",
+                    description="Return the database schema.",
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {},
+                        "additionalProperties": False,
+                    },
+                    strict=True,
+                ),
+            ),
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="query_database",
+                    description="Run a read-only SQL query.",
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {"sql": {"type": "string"}},
+                        "required": ["sql"],
+                        "additionalProperties": False,
+                    },
+                    strict=True,
+                ),
+            ),
+        ]
+        from sglang.srt.function_call.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser
+
+        parser = FunctionCallParser(tools, "qwen3_coder")
+        result = parser.get_structure_constraint("auto")
+        self.assertIsNotNone(result)
+        self.assertEqual(result[0], "structural_tag")
+        self.assertIsInstance(result[1], xgr.StructuralTag)
+
     def test_inkling_auto_constrains_json_after_tool_trigger(self):
         import xgrammar as xgr
